references.text: The Lord makes a distinction between Israel and Egypt by sparing the land of Goshen from the plague of flies, illustrating the same principle of God's protection of His people.
During the hail plague, Goshen where the Israelites lived was spared, yet another example of how the Lord distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.
During the plague of darkness, the Israelites had light in their homes while the Egyptians were in darkness - God makes a distinction between the peoples.
The Lord makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel during the tenth plague; the same Hebrew expression (הִפְלָה) is used.
At Passover, the destroyer passes over the houses of the Israelites - God protects His people and sets them apart from the Egyptians.
The promise that a thousand may fall at the believer's side without harming him illustrates God's protection of His people in the midst of judgment.
You will again see a difference between the righteous and the wicked - the same theme that God distinguishes between His own and others.
A clear theological contrast: Exodus emphasizes God's separation of nations during judgment, while Romans proclaims unity in Christ.
